newsitem.title: FRANCE: WTO chief sees new millennium round gaining ground.
newsitem.headline: WTO chief sees new millennium round gaining ground.

text.p: World Trade Organisation chief Renato Ruggiero said at a meeting of the 29-country OECD on Monday that the idea of a new round of world trade talks at the turn of the century appeared to be gaining some ground.

"There's been some real progress on the idea of a millennium round. It's not for today and it's not for tomorrow but in the perspective of (the year) 2000 there's a certain prospect growing," he told reporters during the two-day OECD meeting.
The annual meeting gathers a mixture of finance, trade, foreign and social affairs ministers from the member states of the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development.

Ruggiero reiterated that China, which made its opening bid to join the WTO's predecessor, the GATT, in 1986, still had some way to go. He also noted that Russia was at the very preliminary stage of a similar process.
"With China I'd say what we have done was very important. (But) There remains a lot to do, especially on market access," he told reporters on the fringes of the OECD meeting.
"With the Russians we're at the beginning," he said.

European Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, who represents the European Union in several trade forums, said Australia and Mexico had agreed to the idea of a new round of WTO talks at the end of the decade.
